note: Muscle MRI studies demonstrate that length-dependent distal-to-proximal fat replacement and an early reticular infiltration pattern distinguish dHMN from distal myopathies presenting with moth-eaten patterns.

evidence.text: A comparative muscle MRI study revealed that a distal-to-proximal gradient of fat replacement and a reticular pattern of fat infiltration were early and exclusive features of dHMN, whereas the moth-eaten pattern predominated in distal myopathies.

source.title: Muscle MRI contributes to the differential diagnosis between distal myopathies and distal hereditary motor neuropathies
source.quote: A length-dependent pattern of muscle involvement, a distal to proximal gradient of fat replacement along the length of the muscles and severe and widespread involvement of foot muscles were more common in patients with dHMNs. Muscle hypertrophy and asymmetry were more frequently observed in the DMs. A reticular pattern of fat infiltration was exclusive to patients with dHMNs, while the moth-eaten pattern predominated in DMs.
